elements.text: கால் மலர்கள் வாடிடினும் அவர் கடும் பயணம் நிற்காது;
கை மலர்கள் பிணைத்து நிற்கும், தம்பியரை, கழகத்தை!
இரு மூன்று திங்கள் வரை சிறையில் வாடி,
அண்ணனுக்கன்றி யாருக்கு வரும் இந்த அழகு நடை?
தனித்தனித் தாய் ஈன்றெடுத்த தம்பிகளே! என அழைத்துக்
கனிச் சுவையாய்க் கற்கண்டாய்த் தேன் பாகாய் அன்பு காட்டிப்
முகில் கிழித்து வெளிக் கிளம்பும் முழு மதியாய்
நிலைகுலையா நம் அண்ணன் அன்று சொன்னார் அது.
தலைவர் இருந்த நாற்காலி, காலியாக இருக்கும்! அதில்
பதுங்கிப் பாயும் வேங்கையெனப் - பாராள வந்த கதை?
சழக்கரால் வீழ்ந்த தமிழ் நிலம் காக்க மன
நச்சுமரம் போலப் பண்பட்ட தமிழர் வாழ்வில் - முதுகில்
சாதிகளைக் காணாது குறள் ஒலித்த தமிழ் மண்ணில்
அழுக்காறு அவர் வெகுளி - இன்னாச் சொல் நான்குமின்றி
பொருள் குவித்து வளம் செழித்த நாட்டில் - இன்று
வாடினாள் தமிழன்னை சோகப் பாட்டுப் பாடினாள் தமிழன்னை;
உழவன் போல் உள்ளமெல்லாம் பூரிப்புத் துள்ளி எழ
அன்பாலே திக்கெட்டும் குறள் பரப்பத் திருவள்ளுவர்க்கும் சிலை
பத்து சிலை வைத்ததனால் - அண்ணன் தமிழின் பால்
நிழல் நீ தான் என்றிருந்தோம்; நீ கடல்
நான்தானடா நன்முத்து எனச் சொல்லிக் கடற்கரையில் உறங்குதியோ?
நாத இசை கொட்டுகின்ற நாவை ஏன் சுருட்டிக் கொண்டாய்?
கண்மூடிக் கொண்டு நீ சிந்திக்கும் பேரழகைப் பார்த்துள்ளேன்
இன்று மண் மூடிக் கொண்டுன்னைப் பார்க்காமல் தடுப்பதென்ன கொடுமை!
இயற்கையின் சதி எமக்குத் தெரியும் அண்ணா... நீ

Kalaignar M. Karunanidhi to Perarignar Anna
More tender than the tenderness of a flower-petal,
a sacred heart — a loving heart —
a mother's heart that gathers one into its embrace! His
even the three fruits, mango, jackfruit and banana, would be defeated —
his eye-flowers become spear, become sword
if any harm should come to Mother Tamil!
Though his foot-flowers wither, his arduous journey will not stop;
his hand-flowers bind together the younger brothers, the Kazhagam!
and make their heads bow in shame like ripened paddy!
Let the flower of democracy sway,
let the flower of social equality spread fragrance,
let the mother tongue Tamil itself become the grove of life —
O flower-crown sought by all! O crown of fame! Amid the heaps
of greetings that come seeking you — each day
I shall fly as the bee that comes singing;
for you I shall give up myself; the great leader
celebrated in the song sung by
Listen, as I sing the greatness
of that man of action and valour, who made
the dear lives of still-young youth swell
with Tamil ardour packed into the drum!
The wounds made by the spear that lodged and burned,
he soothed with the healing heat called love,
and with his red-fruit lips applied medicine —
listen, as I sing that grace!
Where is the sword in the broad battle-hand; where the jewelled chest?
Where, where are the shoulders of the patron
who would never turn his back, whoever came at the battlefront —
listen to how he asked the younger brothers!
while Kanchi stands, Kalinga is lost —
open, that the field-war may be sung!”
To wake the love-bewildered women from sleep,
he set himself to action and sang —
a praise-parani of immeasurable valour — I,
raising a poetic parani, sang a Kanchipuram Parani;
As meaning in poetry, as sweetness in sugarcane,
as light in the sunbeam, as flower in the grove,
as coolness in moonlight, as wealth upon the earth,
as language murmured by a cascading waterfall,
as music mounting the wandering wind,
as foam dancing on the wave-rising sea —
the poet-leader whose gathered art breathes fragrance,
Anna — as I sing his sacred glory,
alas, the tears the Earth-maiden pours!
if some sowed the seed for a language revolution in the motherland,
then under the peerless leadership of
our Anna entered the field, clad in Kanchi!
For two or three months he withered in prison,
giving Tamil as the supporting staff,
and by those rare three letters became Anna....
There is a special glory in three letters,
the fragrance of Muttamil is there...
Three kings, three flags, three fruits —
the Tamils made the three drums resound; the Tamil
`வாழ்வு` — life — they lived has three letters; the
`அன்பு` — love — that is the foundation of that life has three letters...
the `அறிவு` — knowledge — that stands beside love has three letters;
`காதல்` — love — rising among the wise has three letters...
the fierce `வீரம்` — valour — praised by lovers has three letters...
the `களம்` — field — where valour is made to grow has three letters...
the `வெற்றி` — victory — seen upon entering the field has three letters;
who urges us all toward that victory has three letters —
that is what I told you to know!
Tamil thunder to all eight directions,
asking for plans so those without means, those without place,
he circles like a bee, mounting the stage!
every paper, every home is Tamil,
the whole land.... the fragrance of newness is there....
“Hey, younger brother — pick up the pen....!”
“Do not sharpen the knife; sharpen your intellect.”
A treasure-chest of thought, a casket of camphor!
Could we ever forget those heart-winning phrases?
strange thoughts in the hearts of the unemployed —
O King! That is the sign of the times!”
Who but Anna could have such a beautiful gait?
is that not an editorial Tamil Nadu will never forget!
“If this army loses, which army will win?”
“He who has a younger brother fears no army”....
was it not Anna who inscribed them in our hearts!
“Even jasmine from the rival's garden has fragrance” —
what dignity, bearing an opponent's abuse!
As one builds a wall and then paints a picture,
Anna said that politics should be conducted
four or five men sprang about,
could not bear giving birth to everyone,
“Younger brothers born of separate mothers!” he called them,
showing love like fruit-sweetness, sugar-candy, honey-syrup,
and embracing them like a bee settling upon a dewy flower.
The master of speech, Sethu Pillai,
and Somasundara Bharathi — in the battle of words
he made them swoon — poor men; he caught them fast!
The Justice Party, behind the high walls of a fortress —
by his principle that it must not remain
a party of the moneyed caste —
he brought it out into the street!
“Cast away the titles given by the white men,”
he moved the resolution at the Salem conference;
the resolution changing the name to Dravidar Kazhagam
at a conference crowded with the brave!
When Annal Gandhi, following the path of virtue,
Anna rejected Periyar's declaration calling it a day of sorrow
A day of joy! A sweet day!
Indians reduced to bone and skin,
rose, cutting through the fetter of slavery!
“Let us lift the drum of freedom and make it roar” —
that is what Anna said, that very day....
From that day, in the Anna — Ayya — relationship,
in forty-nine it became a separation,
and like a full moon tearing through cloud and emerging,
he made the Munnetra Kazhagam blossom!
Unable to live together with the Leader,
when he came out with the majority of comrades,
our steadfast Anna said it that day.
It feels as though he said it only yesterday!
“There is no leader for the Munnetra Kazhagam —
my Leader's chair will remain empty! In it,
the Leader himself will come and sit someday....
Until then I shall wait,” he said.
Like a flower garden in bloom
those who had waited and heard the meeting
“Drops of tears! Jewels of the nation's eyes!” he called,
and marshalled them to shed red blood!
Has the world ever told it?
like a tiger crouching before its leap — the story of its coming to rule?
Not even two years had passed since my Anna took office —
yet he set about so many distinguished deeds!
to raise all the rich-field farmers
and heap a beautiful life before them.
to inaugurate the World Tamil Conference said,
“I saw an incomparable sight; I saw grandeur;
never in my life have I seen its like,”
and the town itself acclaimed Anna's fame!
“Ah! You alone are the true Gandhian,”
he worshipfully praised him — not even a year had passed!
“You are making prohibition more rigorous; in many states
they have washed their hands of it and tied up the pot;
you alone are the offspring of the Mahatma,” he said.
If Giri means mountain — is it not a mountain among
Our Anna became the cloud embracing the mountain!
This is the explanation of V. V. Giri's greeting.
International scholars stood in praise — that day,
those who had stood as peaks of the South:
The Pallavaram savant of ancient Tamil
stood spellbound by Anna's Tamil speech —
a thousand words of praise from that Maraimalai.
whom the whole land calls Navalar — he said:
“To guard the Tamil land felled by men of crookedness,
we have found a leader without stain in his heart,”
and told Anna's greatness that day!
Two thousand years ago, as young as she is today,
to live for countless crores of years,
gave birth to poets who made thousands of books; yet
our Mother, goddess of the arts,
bore Valluvar as her foremost son.
If flower — it is the lotus;
he gave that book of virtue,
Along the mountain-edge that touches the sky —
rising within and beyond our sight —
like a poisonous tree, in the cultivated life of Tamils,
alas, doctrines wounded in the back began to blaze!
On Tamil soil where the Kural rang out without seeing castes,
midway came crores upon crores of castes!
and temples housing a thousand gods took their place.
Creatures with only appetite of mouth, with no feeling for language —
whether Tamil died or lived, what did it matter to them?
On the great land where the path of virtue had stood as the goal,
they sowed other paths; they heaped up errors.
Like a field gone without rain, the Tamil mind was changed;
envy, `avar`, anger, hurtful speech — without those four,
some Tamils went about as though no work could be done!
“For those without wealth, there is no world,” they said,
and in a land that had amassed wealth and flourished — today
darkness gathered and distress planted its flag.
Mother Tamil withered; Mother Tamil sang a song of sorrow;
Mother Tamil danced in burning fire...
She ran... she ran... no path could be found!
Leaving the town of earth, he lives in the town of fame —
the great sovereign of poetry's city, the master of the Kural!
She went to him and said, “Dear son!
“What is it, Mother?” asked the Kural-master.
“In Tamil Nadu, where gold comes wherever one digs,
you must be born again,” she said.
“To make the minds and lives of Tamils
She said danger threatened the mountain-like language;
he said the poor had no hut to go to;
not knowing how to raise the rod swiftly and cast it gently,
“the killing staff has risen high,” she said; and told him too
the idle stories told by calves in intellect.
Wiping the eyes that had wept,
Kissing the crown of the worshipful son's head,
with arms like hanging banyan roots, she held him close.
“A ploughed field must not dry for want of seedlings —
not from now on,” she thought;
her whole heart leapt full with joy
like a farmer whose mind is glad.
“To pour gruel into the dried stomach —
O sugar-candy! O honey-syrup! O Tirukkural!
be born in Kanchi!” she said.
He was born as our Anna;
As the breeze from Pothigai Hill,
as the meaning of a hymn
as the war-song of the ancient Tamils,
as the fresh fragrance of Tamil consciousness,
a ray risen in the eastern sky —
I too, the younger brother he nurtured,
taking the Tamil he gave me,
have come here; this is the truth —
they call him Leader, they call him philosopher,
they call him actor, they call him king of drama,
they say he possessed savour-rich power of speech and writing.
They call him human, they call him a jewel, they call him
they call him mother, guardian of noble speech,
they call him politician — and those who have no time
to say each one separately — let them, in their hearts,
call him by the one word “Anna” —
To honour that clan of mothers:
a statue for Kannagi who nurtured virtue,
a statue for Bharathi of the unbending heart,
a statue for Bharathidasan of the unbowed crown,
a statue for Caldwell and Pope,
a statue for the valiant Tamil who steered the ship,
a statue for Tiruvalluvar, to spread the Kural with love to all eight directions.
Because he placed ten statues — so the world might know
a statue for that Anna himself
We thought our Anna was issuing an order.
Alas — today alone do we understand
“I shall live only one more year!”
“You have a younger brother who fears no army,”
why did you leave us and continue the great journey....?
We grew in the warmth of the light of your eyes!
Why did you turn all our eyes into pools?
We thought you were our shade; but you have gone
beneath the sea-land seeking shade — is that justice?
Not every pearl beneath the sea is a pearl;
are you sleeping on the shore saying, “I alone am the good pearl, my boy”?
Why did you roll up the tongue that poured out music?
With a movement of your finger,
you made wonders in the world of letters;
why did you fold that finger away?
I have seen the great beauty of you thinking with eyes closed;
today what cruelty is this earth closing over you, barring us from seeing you!
You brought cruelty to an end; why did you go,
You said we needed a heart that could bear anything;
where, Anna, is the heart in us to bear even this!
Enough of taking the sea breeze on the shore, Anna!
You will not come; you will not come;
we know nature's conspiracy, Anna... until
I come seeking the place where you are,
When I come, I shall bring it with me in my hands
and place it at your flower-feet, Anna......

Short beard; squat beard; long beard; white beard;
with beards of every kind like these...
a crowd of pūsuras, spreading out a bazaar of Puranas,
tasting the sour old grove, getting drunk and dancing.
At the edge of a realm once without stain or blemish,
they slaughtered cows, goats and human beings,
heaping mounds of corpses for sacrifice!
by a swaying waist... a sidelong glance... by the sages'
wine of pleasure — in the southern land gone dark —
If I begin to tell his history... every muscle dances, ayyo!
The lord of southern Lanka whose fame reached all eight directions,
Our grandfather who held fast to love of ancient Tamil.
The island of Lanka like the pupil within the eye,
the deep seas its dark iris! The great warrior
who brought renown to Tamil soil.
A lion in form, a heart of gold! He lived
with none his equal in the mode of the yāzh —
a man of sacred Jaffna, a mountain-Tamilian!
His companion, flower-tressed where bees would settle,
Mandodari — jewel of womankind — a speaker
whose words could pluck an answering veena!... Ravana's yāzh-music
was defeated only before the fruit-sweet speech
of his chaste wife in the bedchamber!
There are eyelid-doors to guard beautiful eyes;
In the forests, along our border-lines, Aryans
sought sacrifice for their god; saying
such cruelty must not be, he drew his sword!
Invitations from forest hermitages kissed his feet;
the laughter of those young women flowered like a palmyra spathe!
"Ha! Would I touch an Aryan scorpion?"
That bull raised a cry of resistance!.....
Wherever foxes filled the forest, wherever deceivers roamed the land:
Ravana was the cock that announced the hour! The cock!
blew the conch against the ascetics of Dandakaranya!
She sprang forth like a vengai, a woman of a warrior clan;
the Ganges seemed to stream from the eyes of the Veda-chanters!
Having understood that strength of shoulder could not
defeat the Tamils, they turned to treachery and intrigue:
with the younger Lakshmana and Sita, his wife, following behind,
the king called Rama set out,
a man who, after wronging his brother and seeking the crown,
was scorned throughout the land as a betrayer of trust
and had gone away to the forest!
as he wandered by the forest, sugarcane-like Muthunagai
slept from weariness beside an orchard of fruit trees.
The vile man, his reason lost to lust,
went near the pure woman sleeping with lotus eyes closed,
intending wickedly to violate her — his younger brother
Sita Devi stood there as a ready hand for guard!
Muthunagai, who had fallen asleep without a guard,
flared up to protect the fire of her chastity...
one woman alone like a fruit tree — against two monkeys!
As the price of chastity she lost a hand! Lost her nose!
Lost the teeth that scattered Muthunagai's pearls! Alas,
lost her breast — yet her chastity
A Tamil woman who would guard honour even if her head were lost,
The ear-burning news that a guileless sister
had been made into Surpanakha reached him —
he looked as though a wound had opened in his eye.
The king who ruled sea-girt earth — was he not
Even if there were no spreading bond of kin,
was she not a citizen of Lanka?
storing in his eyes the redness of the young morning sun...!
Hearing that the king was coming, beautiful-eyed Sita Devi
and sent her husband racing after it!
"In the elder brother's absence, do you think
to cast a net for your sister-in-law, younger brother?
Run after the elder one, you too!" — she drove him away
and waited for the Southerner to arrive.
With eyes throwing sparks, the warrior came like a chariot.
He saw Sita, pouring honeyed speech, come to the street entrance.
"The elder and younger have both run away —
you, the one suited to me, have now come —
I give myself to you," she said,
and twined herself around Ravana's broad shoulders,
green-bangled Sita Devi like a spreading jasmine creeper!
"You are the wife of the man who harmed
Rather than give your body to crow and vulture
I will not even let my hand touch it.
The companion of the man born in a lineage
that had loaded its honour upon a ship said,
and leaned upon his strong chest —
thinking that somehow she would gain the boon,
she boarded the vessel and stood,
a she-fox behind the lion of proud gait!
"If he carries Sita Devi away as prisoner,
sets her upon the throne and makes her crowned queen,

They lived in prison; they pulled the oil-press —
to drive out the white rulers of this land,
many received shortened lives and suffered killing.
Like a sword leaping out beyond its sheath,
without attachment to life, they fought.
On this day when we have assembled to speak their greatness,
to speak the greatness of all who gave their lives for freedom,
I do not possess poetic wealth like these men;
I have not learned to sing poetry.
But because I sing the story of warriors who broke shackles,
because they slapped their thighs and felled traitors,
my song too slaps its thigh!
go without *yāppu* if it must — but our country,
even if I have had no opportunity to study prosody,
I will not stand like a tree that never bears fruit;
I turn the feelings soaking my heart into lines
and say one thing for the axes that change their principles to understand:
How many lives, how much blood,
given without end to win freedom!
After digging this earth and labouring so greatly,
after obtaining gold of ten-and-a-half purity,
is it right, instead of showing craft,
and giving it to women like paintings,
to throw it into a rubbish pit?
In a grove where birds cry,
a fine rose plucked while thorns scratched —
upon the heads of sword-bearing warriors,
in the hair of modest women,
to the cramped fist of a wicked monkey?
We shall cherish and protect the freedom we won;
we shall add honour to the warriors who won it.
If one or two relatives alone
live in prosperity — is that freedom?
those who toil in the fields,
for all to delight in a life free of evil:
let us sound it today in rhythmic Tamil.
We have spoken of the greatness of your lion-sons;
so that Tamilakam may reap victory everywhere,
grant us your grace here, Mother!

Elders of this great college assembly,
Receive my greetings with hearts in which a mother's love grows,
as I come to sing Tamil that bows to no enemy,
on the five senses — body, mouth, eye, nose and ear.
He said with his mouth that it was a poetry gathering;
my whole body thrilled — had they really counted me a poet?
He winked and said yes — perhaps it was a joke!
I seized it and read it — with my eyes, of course!
A small treatment for the nose injured in a car accident;
I stayed silent, wondering whether I could go.
My friend did not let go.
in my ear I heard Rahman's voice.
He invited me by mouth and thrilled my body,
sent a letter for my eyes to see,
and though there was illness in Kalaignar's nose,
said he would not let me off even three-quarters of the way;
without minding expense he called by telephone to cool my ear.
After all that, if I failed to come,
I tied up this unopened bud of poetry
I came in the evening believing it would bloom by evening!
They say one beautiful moon makes the lily bud bloom;
here there are five or six beautiful poet-moons,
so surely even the bud I brought will bloom?
If it does not, blame the moon;
blame those who thought me a poet.
In North Arcot, where colourful hills stand,
there is a friend, a jasmine branch in my grove of friendship,
whose heart trembled whenever trouble came to me —
When coming here there was no holding me back;
“They say the body dances and subsides,
therefore controlling the five senses is good.”
Will the ear reject the song of the green bird?
Will the body reject the embrace of the green parrot?
Will the mouth refuse to speak ancient Tamil?
Will the eye reject a moon like a jackfruit segment?
Will the nose reject the fragrance of a dew-wet flower?
All those great sages of the worlds
who performed penance to subdue the five senses —
Viswamitra gave up throne and jewelled crown
and lived as an ascetic in the forest;
do you not know how he became Menaka's faithful friend?
Likewise, when eye, ear, nose, mouth and body —
the five senses — ran like unbridled horses,
like a flood in a wild river,
with wounded body and lamenting mouth.

You who have come on stage,

In this college hall, those who let poetry mount the stage

Poets! When you argue that your chosen subject is the greatest,
if the body is too large, people call it an elephant;
if the eye is too large, an owl;
if the nose is too large, a capsicum;
if the mouth is too large, they say chatterbox;
if the ear is too large, they mutter “winnowing tray.”
So speak of your subject knowing the proper measure.
If trouble comes, I shall ward it off;
if trouble comes among poets, I shall rejoice!
Take up the staff of Tamil and play a duel of words;
take up arrows of verse and attack one another;
at the same time, take up ripened love and support one another.
Taste, light, touch, sound and smell —
expound the kinds of the five.
Put enmity, blame, victory and boast in your poems;

A little cockfight is for money;
a king's fight is for a country;
the fight we watch is for Tamil.
First, on the theme of the body —

Without the body there is no eye, no nose,

That is — is it true that he is going to say that?

Between the debate over truth and falsehood,
let us hear Sahul Hameed's Tamil.

In a land that drapes poets in silk,

has woven a silk cloth and draped us all.
We listened to songs roaring as they attacked one another.
If the moon and Ganga quarrel
upon Siva's red matted hair adorned with konrai,
it becomes a headache for Siva;
this poets' fight is a battlefield fight —
a fight joined with Tamil rock-candy!
The one who said the body is greatest will not wish to live without a mouth;
the one who said the mouth is greatest will not wish to be deaf;
the one who praised the beauty of the eye will not dare reduce the beauty of the nose;
and will the one who praised the nose say, “I will go about bumping into things without eyes?”
Those who climbed this stage and sang possess all of them.
So is this a useless quarrel?
No — it is a quarrel of vīṇā-Tamil,
If this quarrel takes place throughout the country,
learning will grow; novelty will arise;
As long as breath passes through the nose,
Even after it ceases, guard Tamil through your fame.
Turn everything the eye sees into poetry;
turn it into poetry of awakening,
and begin the duty of putting it into action —
begin the duty, begin the duty!
Hear what is good with the ear; cast away what is not;
open the mouth to sing the welfare of classical Tamils.
Even if you say only one thing, say a good thing.
If a body exists without all I have said,
then that body is not *mey* — truth — but *poi*, falsehood.

Let us wish that people everywhere in the world
may live without riots and without rancour.
Though I say the year's birth is in Thai,
this has entered common practice, so let us offer greetings.
Why practise such thrift in blessing,
blessing only one day in a whole year?
With full mouth and full heart I will bless on many days,
and I greet the poets who have come to sing on the radio.
Sleep has broken; long eyes have opened.
The maiden Chithirai, a golden woman bearing a seal,
and learned Valluvar whom this earth praises —
let us enter the Kural he composed
and taste the thought it offers here.
There is no fame merely by birth;
fame comes from the excellence one earns —
so he sang in the Book of Virtue.
Good people have come to open that book in song
so that we do not forget it.
I am a bird that does not fly,
a chick of poetry distressed because wings of grammar have not sprouted;
a bird that does not fly,
a bird that does not fly from nest to nest,
a poetry chick whose wings have not sprouted —
let only a tail not sprout, as it has for some!
That is the little poet I call myself.
Do not think I say this from modesty.
Feet, metre, linkage, ornament and prosody —
all of them only block my song!
You must grant me an exemption;
otherwise I shall rise saying I must walk away from you.
One day while asleep I saw a dream.
Do not ask, “Then what — do dreams come while awake?”
Gandhi dreamed while awake and won freedom;
Anna, smiling through the abuse of many,
dreamed while awake of good government,
What was this servant's sleeping dream?
beauties whom anyone would long to drink in with the eyes.
South of the village called Honey-Pond,
under the shade beside the public tank,
I sat in a car with my eyes closed in sleep.
“We are jackfruits held within the root;
is there anywhere in the world a maiden like us?” they said.

live your life rejoicing with her.
time is passing without interest!” they said.
“Are you girls from a Chettiar household?” I asked.
“There is no caste that butts and clashes, no religion —

All six had one complexion, one nature,
in the twin fruit trees upon their dew-flower bodies,
in the grace of their walk,
in the spear-army of their eyes,
in the shopfront of their lips,
there was no contradiction; even their smiles were one.
If one woman's body was silk,
If one spoke the path of grace,
if one spoke in the language of the Kural,
What was I to do? How could I choose?
With spear-eyes they wounded my heart,
made music in my chest for love,
and by a wonder that made earth itself,
plucked out my eyes and left me suffering in confusion.
Very well, I thought: ask their names,
then choose the one we want.
If self-control is present, grace comes dancing;
where sweet speech lives, forbearance reigns;
becomes a thumbai-grove where non-harm flowers.
Only the names differ — what else differs?
“Good women of equal age, equal nature, equal face —
who is the mother who bore you?” I asked.
I shall bring six poets here.
After hearing the poems they speak,
you may garland them and rejoice,” I said.
They agreed, and the poets arrived.

With the dream shattered, I came to this poetry gathering.
The poet who broke the dream, Soundara Kailasam,

So, since it is good for her now to speak to the assembly,

The lady will thunder on the theme “Sweet Speech.”

We say feet are for walking, not kicking!

a knife is needed to cut fruit, not take life.

the loud courage of the tongue is counterfeit courage.

The eye restrained at the eyelid-door;
the tongue restrained in the prison of the mouth;
the body restrained in the grave;
a good mind restrained in the light of reason.
To thank those who ordered me to preside is assembly-modesty;
to bless those who begged me to preside would be swelling of the head.
“Guard the tongue, whoever you are” — the first step of restraint;
to keep a “mad dog” inside the mouth is the upper stair of arrogance.
If it rolls out from there, the heart-pressure itself may collapse without form!
To offer all this in the assembly,
The crescent waits and becomes the moon;
those with forbearance wait and come to rule the land.
The crane waits until prey comes;
it is strategy the bird learned upon the earth.
The one who makes enduring insult the highest virtue,
Valluvar said, is like earth that bears those who dig it.
Those who insult possess neither true greatness
nor the art of scribbling abuse.

Learned elders seated in the middle of this assembly,
and poets of distinction who have come with Tamil-rich verse
to show six figures from the noble scripture, the Tirukkural —
Twelve months, and four more beyond that —

at five or six poetry gatherings

They did not invite me out of indulgence saying I was a poet.
Even a spinning top, after circling, lies down;
I roll from town to town like a kicked ball.
Though the body has grown lean,
life itself has not grown weak;
you climb my body, climb my life and keep me living;
I have no wish to oppose grammar.
Grammar itself is the beloved child that sulks with me.
Even if not one of my songs agrees with grammar,
I have the courage that the song I give will not kill Tamil feeling.
Like a neem twig entering a sugarcane mill,
I have bravely entered this gathering of poets.
In this flower-garden where rare songs bloom,
your rare songs become flowers in Tamil's garland;
you are bees dancing around them;
I am only a splinter moving among you!
If an ant can move an iron pillar,
if an ant can make an iron pillar move,
then even my bare song can defeat you!
V. K. C. Natarasan, worthy organiser
who founded Tamil Vattam and conducts this Tamil festival,
Because he invited me with affection,
I said I must come lest he circle around me again.
A *vattam* — circle — is a name for classification,
a component that works to a plan.
The dot on a maiden's forehead is a circle;
the moon pouring light is a circle;
the far-raying sun is a circle;
and the marks some students receive are a complete zero!
For the act of love, the bed is a circle;
for the sweet-speaking child, the cradle is a circle;
for women's life, chastity's path is a circle;
for warriors' greatness, the battlefield is a circle;
for the farmer's plough, the field is a circle;
for a friend's relationship, the house of love is a circle;
for the ascetic's purity, the mind-cage is a circle;
for the base man's life, the circle is unknown —
only after seeing him do we arrive at the title “base man.”

Do not live in anger — increase the farming clan!”

Why a separate explanation for a minister?
If he does not fear enemies, he becomes a warrior;
if he does not fear blame, he becomes a base man;
in showing love, he becomes a woman.
More than ploughing with a good plough,

if he gives up the comforts that come, he becomes an ascetic;

For a woman, greatness lies in guarding herself;
for a warrior, in the honour-wound;
for an ascetic, in the grave;
for a base man, in every greatness he happens to see;
for the potter, an earthen pot!
My greatness is simply to be here among you.
If that greatness remains, it is enough for me.

They told me, “Are you not related to the water family?”

rain's writing upon earth becomes river;

The root-letter of all these, they say, is the sea.
One man grieves, “What fate is written on my head?”

If I said that thunder is the old man of the sky coughing,
lightning the light from his swollen eyes,

So I shall offer an image young people may like:
the fish of the sky are women;
the sword-like sweep of their eyes is the lightning-streak;

when great warriors' spears scrape — lightning;
when many warriors pour red water — rain.
In general the sky itself is a battlefield —

There is no Godavari in Tamil Nadu —
there is no line of caste coming here as “gothra-varisai”!
No Godavari for the dry field in Tamil Nadu;
for Tamils abroad, there is a place to live —
We bow to you, river — live long.
They called me here for six topics,

Next, let us go to the well.
I am a frog in the well of the village of poetry.
I do not know the abundance of song as you do, sir!
If the long sky refuses rain,
if long river, pond and pool dry and wither,
if not even a cup of water remains to quench thirst,
then, as one swallows one's own saliva,
a deep well, a riverbank well.
People say, “When a well is dug, a ghost comes out.”
Do you understand what that means?
Dig a well and earth piles up — one element;
the air trapped under the ground comes out — another;
fresh water wells up — the next;
the bright sky appears upon the water — the fourth;
and the sun's fiery rays purify that water — the fifth.
It is the arrival of these five elements
that the old people expressed beautifully;
A pond gives beauty to a village;
I too have a pond — a heart — for poetry,
and I have a heart for public service.
The lotus pond is great beauty;
the hidden pond is the Tirukkural;
the heart of scripture is the Tirukkural.
there are tanks that have taken some lives.

Every pond needs a stone bathing-step;

Singing this, I climb out of the pond.
The sea is vast on earth;
the river has great fame in the world;
the well too has many honours;
all ponds are nectar-mouths of the globe.
But all of them arise only when the cloud-cluster sheds tears:
rivers run, wells spring, ponds fill.
The tears shed by the morning flower are dew;
the tears shed by the coconut spathe are toddy;
the poor man's tears become a spear,
“Are not the tears shed by those
the army that wears away wealth?”
So let us turn swiftly from tears to sweat.
In an oyster's sweat a pearl is born;
in a sculptor's sweat a statue is born;
in a farmer's sweat hunger flies away;
in a warrior's sweat the enemy flies away.
The sweat of the powerful is rosewater;
the sweat of the humble is red water.
In the furnace, flame drinks the sweat that falls;
every drop of sweat becomes sandal paste and perfume.
When poets of distinction are here
from the broad sea down to the pond of sweat,
is it right for me alone to sing so much?

at the Pari festival on Parambu Hill
“A Walking Journey for Tamil to Flourish.”
Every Tamil art sings of culture!
Every wave of the sea dances!
Every cluster of enemies trembles and runs!
In the forest where peaks rise,
where swift creatures run and play,
where proud herds of deer move,
where paired cuckoos sing their music,
where forest peacocks spread rhythm and expression,
where silk banners and victory parasols turn and whirl —
let us worship the fame of generous Pari,
who poured out bounty like a flood,
and who received the circling radiance
You have given us the apt title “walking journey”
and made a way for the Tamil people,
Let us labour without weariness every day
Are we not a pride of lions?
Shall we bow our heads to the howling of jackals?
shall the base make a show of bravado?
Does he stand like a vertical pillar,
without courage to oppose the degradations here?
with no pulse in his limbs?
write a song about him for the Sangam!
Set up a golden statue for him!
like two chisels laid above the lips,
that humiliation never came to him.
as though crying the same racial call.
like the swinging trunk of an elephant.

recover the feeling of the Tamils of old.
you will sing of eight paths.

Those who make a habit of striking us
for as long as we remain bent.
at some of the paths we can reach.
but the finest path of friendship,
whose palanquin, sceptre, chariot and army
had been defeated on the battlefield,
to his friend who had ruled a land,
who, if a friend is dying,
hurry to place a stone upon his head!
For all of them to change their path,
old Avvai, walking with a staff,
taught paths by which the sceptre of rule
a good path by which the Tamil people may prosper.
and will enemies dare enter the heart and come near?
The path by which Ilango renounced household life
through which he gave Tamils a noble ethic.
So too is the path of Vallalar Adigal.
The path that framed pearl-like principles —
that is the path of Arignar Anna!
Let us give them the way;
let us receive their sweet words.
I heard that Adigalar wishes to perform virtue.
Like me, his head is bald.
Is not a tender coconut bald too?
Ilanchera, one of my own kind,
and makes poems like clusters of fruit —
a Pandyan comes to sell an anklet.
“To walk the path, we need the feet of Appar;
to walk the path, we need Appar's feet” —
is the path proper to humankind,
Mudiyarasu, who studies melody and sings,
now studies Anna's path and sings.
They have told us eight paths.
the road our Anna laid down for us.

in the lap of the mother
who carried and gave birth to me;
the joy I did not find
on the shoulders of the father
who lifted me and raised me;
the joy I did not find
the joy I did not find
in the affection of the companions
the joy I did not find
in the speech of my children,
speech that defeats flute and yāzh
and even the Kural that praises them —
you treat it as an order,
Before my lips can even move
Those who know my path know:
it is the path of Periyar and Anna.
Yet how many crores of taunts,
this heart has carried and carried,
Not every stone struck by a chisel
becomes a sculpture alive with spirit.
to those who carved me into one!
is shaped into sword or spear.
a mere sandal beneath the foot,
that would again make the land
parties lose the human being himself,
and reel from scene to changing scene.
this is the vow I take:
of the people of our race,
without even an atom of time

elements.text: முன் தோன்றி மூத்த குடியின் பழம்பாட்டே! இன்று
மா, பலா, வாழைத் தமிழே! நீ வாழ்க நன்று!
பாம்பைக் கண்டால் பிறகு அடி என்று சொன்னார்
அவள் பெற்ற அழுக்குப் பிள்ளைக்கு உயிர் கொடுக்க
தீரமிகு பணிகள் பல ஆற்றியவர் பெரியார் அன்றோ?
பொங்குற்ற வேங்கை போல் நிமிர்கின்ற பார்வை உண்டு
பம்பரமும் ஓய்வு பெறும் சுற்றிய பின்! - இவரோ
ஏன் என்று கேட்பதிலே வைர நெஞ்ச வால்டேராய்
பருவோடு சண்டை போட்டால் நம் முகம்தான் கெடும்
பரவாயில்லை என்று புனுகு போட்டால் பரு உதிரும்.
பாக்குக்கும் வெற்றிலை சுண்ணாம்புக்கும் அவர் வாய் சிவக்கும்
நமக்கென்ன வந்த தென்று விதிவிலக்குப் பெற்ற வீரரல்ல!
ஓடி ஒளிந்த மனிதர் சிலர் இன்று ஒழிக்கின்றேன் இந்தியை என்று
அவசர காலச் சட்டத்தின்போது இந்திக்கே ஆதரவு என்று
கண்ணீர் விடும் விவசாயி கனற்பிழம்பாய் மாறி விட்டால்
இப்பெரும் நாடு காக்க நமது மொழி காக்க
Tamil, granted to us as life itself!
Even the moon bears a stain,
you are a ray of light without blemish!
what we need in the conch-resounding battlefield
Laugh so the whole land shakes:
let talk of defeat belong henceforth
to the enemy, not to us!
have come to divide up Tamil life into shares.
The Tamil host must gather without bank or boundary.
We must make the blind and mute awaken and speak,
and make them march toward the field.
you are the *purappāttu* living in our word and deed,
the ancient song of the elder people
who arose before stone and earth,
unvanquished even by the sea's engulfing flood —
the Tamil of mango, jackfruit and banana,
giving flavour to the new song I sing today.
We have seen the three great seas,
seen the glory of the three Sangams,
now let us behold the Three Great Celebration!
when we do not think of Anna,
Today let us take a vow
to guard the policy that is our very eye.
Gold? Wealth? What use are they?
Erode was once like a head full of lice;
had there been no Erode comb
might by now have gone bald!
He never worried about stars either.
it must surely have been Leo!
jackals could not wag their tails.
its lava rushed toward the citadel of Vedic orthodoxy.
in it the great serpents of Sanatana order
He was a wild flood breaking its banks;
the mud houses of old almanacs
can make ruin hard to stop,
he was the Periyar — the great river!
If that river rises in anger,
will not the taproots of epic and purana
making the red dawn itself blush,
Crores of young bulls of modernity
our blood itself is the stake.
The man of this land shall live here,
a man of fame who can outshine any land.
The Tamil who had bowed his head —
A new idea arose — a revolutionary idea.
If even a worm becomes a tiger when trodden on,
Yet some still do not understand!
to run and play in streets
Yet the last Shudra or Panchama,
said to have been born from the god's feet,
becomes pollution merely by walking there.
Such was the unjust “justice” called Manu's law,
with no one to reject it
before Periyar was born in Erode.
and the skull of that bitter doctrine
for Bama and Radha and all their kind,
you conduct marriage festivals every year.
“What became of last year's marriage, ayya?”
Who has yet answered that question of reason?
gathered the dirt from her body,
and stationed that form as guard
Shiva, who had swallowed the deadly poison,
The form stopped him as a man.
and struck off the dirt-born figure's head.
Parvati, seeing it, blazed in fury
to restore life to the child born of her dirt.
An elephant happened along the street;
and fixed upon the dirt-born body.
You know it, do you not?
If Mother Parvati carried enough dirt on her body
to make such a large child,
how many days must she have gone without bathing?
Was it not the old man of Erode
and turned purana into an object of ridicule?
who cleared the weeds of ideas,
saying that the crop of common ownership
can grow only in a social field
from which weeds have been removed?
You who measure and declare that an “atma” exists —
where then did the tale of the next birth come from?
There is no ghost, no demon — madmen!
Who lit the Self-Respect flame saying,
“Do not believe what swindlers tell you”?
Why did he affectionately call Kamaraj
So the backward classes might live!
that Kazhagam rule should continue for all time?
So that the dreams he had seen
might be fulfilled step by step!
lying like the Lord of Srirangam,
spring up and thunder in all eight directions
Street stage, art stage, music stage, cinema stage —
made it a Tamil stage, a stage of our own.
Is it not fitting to hold a poetry assembly
for the man who did so?
He had a beard like Tagore of Bengal,
a gaze raised like a charging tiger,
a body like a red hill,
and in eyes white as conch
light remained in them until death.
Even a spinning top rests after circling;
he, even in extreme old age,
still went round like a top.
as the great torch of ethnic consciousness,
as a sharp sword cutting down degradation,
as Ingersoll who denied even God,
as Socrates forever speaking in Athens,
as Voltaire with a diamond heart asking “Why?” —
and filled every atom of our thought!
A rain of reason would fall —
for Kazhagam people it was like eating *adhirasam*;
for villains, like an atom bomb exploding!
he lived to fullness of age and then rested.
Yet if the Taj Mahal suddenly sank into the earth,
by saying, “It was built many years ago”?
would it be easy to bear
by saying it had grown old?
He was as tall as the Thanjavur tower,
a maker of history like the Taj Mahal.
A hundred years for that sun of awakening!
Can a storm wind give birth
a breeze that drove away even violent storms
he classified the greatness in which we had once lived
and gave us a deep treasury of ideas.
It was a treasury of thought —
not some broken-eared chest imagined by a black-money man
but a camphor casket given by Kanchi Anna!
as a motorboat carrying the poor in knowledge to shore,
as a sunbeam forgiving the errors of the small,
as a master who made fanatics bow,
he conducted politics with method and principle
and planned the removal of the begging bowl.
Some who once sat with “Sri” before their names
now wander the street abusing us.
If we fight a pimple, our own face is spoiled;
apply civet calmly and the boil will fall away.
Even when he differed in thought from E. V. R. Periyar
and wept as he parted to form another Kazhagam,
our Anna thundered to the enemy
that the two would remain like a double-barrelled gun.
to rip open the womb of the mother herself;
It feels as though it happened today —
that sight of the cow parting from the Kazhagam calf.
As though a spear that could pierce a hill
was aimed and tore our chest,
Anna, who would never leave us,
Eight or nine years have passed.
Avvai has a song called *Kondrai Vendhan*;
our king of principle has an imperishable song!
He showed in his new Tamil style
both the gait of the swelling sea
and the soft walk of maidens.
He trapped those who spoke evil in debate.
At the moment of taking snuff,
with a smile he ground his opponents to powder.
He drove out those of dusty character.
He placed a golden crown on Mother Tamil.
to alter the fate written on the heads
Betel, areca and lime reddened his mouth;
if Hindi came to strike Tamils,
and let “assembly president” walk the stage.
Once a flag-hoisting ceremony exists in pure Tamil,
If “Truth alone triumphs” is said in Tamil,
cannot be conducted in Tamil nurtured by the Sangam!
To meet the battle method of the Kanchi seat,
the leader from Kanchi did not leave us untaught.
If worship for the Lord in the temple
cannot be in the mother tongue,
we shall beat the drum and say:
we do not need that Lord either!
We are brothers to the young breeze called Anna;
we are grandchildren of the great storm called Periyar.
Those who impose the northern language
If they tread on the feet
the head of language domination — take warning!
We are soldiers of a forty-year language war,
by saying, “What has it to do with us?”
and flowered as corpses in the middle of the street,
and became lamps that cannot be extinguished,
some who luckily escaped the nationwide earthquake
and purchase valour at market price.
Even a party that sang off-key
in support of Hindi during the Emergency
now says Hindi must not come.
When cats themselves roar like leopards,
if we leopards rise in anger,
will there not be a war that shakes the earth?
for a Kazhagam man these are old stories!
as long as even one Tamil remains alive,
if they come to strike iron pillars!
you may run the country as you please.
they would have stood as dams
You might then have escaped without melting away.
Beating one's chest before a bull without a nose-rope
Even Anna, who asked us to be patient
like earth that bears those who dig it,
Is it not jungle rule that continues?
they think the Kazhagam will tremble
“I shall drive out the liquor demon.”
Is he some demon without a form
laughing as an organiser of the ruling party!
proof exists by the thousand, one upon another.
We would need a separate poetry assembly
they act like Buddha and Jesus
and ask us to believe them!
Have you ever heard ministers before
the carts will certainly be smashed,
turns into a spark of fire,
to be a sack of gooseberries,
the pressure in the chest grows.
When will the domination of evil men
I know the question that rises.
There is black soil in the land,
if the enemy's feet must be washed,
they race ahead to do it.
is like the pleasure of prostitutes
who embrace a man's corpse for money!
how can they bear their principles?
and raise the cry of the people;
Ayya lit the lamp of reason.
Again a great wind blows today.
lakhs, crores of hands stretch out.
All of them are Anna's hands.
`Agaram` is the first letter of Tamil;
Anna's name is the first letter for Tamils.
That leader of the first letter gave us
the Munnetra Kazhagam — the Progressive Federation.
If progress is to reach Tamils,
the Three Great Celebration alone is not enough.
today itself we must take a vow.
We must understand Perarignar Anna's clarity.
We need firmness that does not fear great opposition.
Death comes at six or at a hundred —
We need a heart of sacrifice
that does not count the sweetness of life.
We must open a brave chest
We need the resolve of the revolutionary poet:
a prison that thinks it can cage us.”
We must move as warriors of fighting spirit.
Periyar and Anna must live forever

Under the title **“In a Changing Town,”**
Puducherry Radio arranged an Independence-Day poetry assembly
six poets sang on the sub-themes
This is the presiding poem he delivered.
to the Honourable Chief Minister of Puducherry,
to the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Assembly,
who plans and carries out his tasks,
who would give even their lives
to the elders of rich Tamil
who have come to hear this radio *kaviyarangam*;
who have come to sing in many modes.
In the land where the volcanic poet of Ettayapuram
the poet who made an earthquake of revolution,
we have gathered for a poetry assembly of freedom
that cuts away the destroying chains of slavery.
the benefit of our own rule
has not reached all who suffer.
poor people lie here and there
When will the tongue praise this
no house in which to shelter.
the insects and worms of the drain?
only so that self-respect might disappear?
loving people who worship in Allah's name
rushed out of line to receive charity.
In the cruel mortar of death
struck by the pestle called crowding,
They ran seeking veshtis and saris,
they bloomed as plants of death.
to see crops like those of barren soil?
so that a few may live
Let us at least now make a rule
so those who have nothing may live
the supposed fruits of previous birth.
break down the fortress of domination
like a flood from an opened sluice.
Puducherry Radio has built this assembly
from this waterfall of honeyed taste!
where I died and lived again!
where many bathe in sacred water,
They lifted me and threw me into a drain.
Because the mosquitoes of death did not bite,
and made me bear new trials.
Had it swallowed me that day,
I would have no trouble at all today!
is there a greatness of newness?
a tiger-cub rests in its mother's lap;
in the grove a cuckoo sings;
The talk that birth makes one high or low
has been destroyed by the secretion of reason —
Yet people do not forget division,
and religions do not renounce collision.
They let equality dance on the stage,
then secretly plot to break its leg,
“It is God's doing — what can we do?”
Strike such a crowd with the whip!
already broken by labour upon labour?
They bake in the forge's hot fire;
they die in the deep mud of the field;
they perish among waves without fearing storms.
They strike rocks to lay good roads.
Yet sweet sermons are preached at them:
how much more must they labour and tear themselves apart?
people worn out by ceaseless work
advice and sermons are bundles of wet firewood;
they cannot cook the socialism we need.
so these do not become empty exteriors,
we must understand the greatness of labour
and establish equality without high and low.
even an onion will take Draupadi's vow,
Even an onion takes Draupadi's vow.
a lump of mud praises itself as Karna.
so is the clod Karna too?
in the temple it will make a commotion:
Not every oil-press stone becomes a Sivalinga!
a man who eats six times every day
he eats until sweat from his forehead falls to the ground!
I call the poets steeped in Tamil.
you whose metrical chains caress the ear,
whose beauty surpasses an ivory statue,
whose heart is filled with delightful Tamil,

தெருப் புழுதியில் கிடந்தாலும் குன்றிமணி நிறம் குன்றாதென்று

சிறு துளி தான் பெரு வெள்ளம்.... ஒவ்
வொரு துளியும் விஷத் துளியாய் இருத்தல் நன்றோ?
கலை கற்று நிலை கெட்டு நிற்போர் தான் - நல்ல
ஆடு, மாடு, பன்றி முதல் கழுதை வரை
சமுதாயத்தில் அன்று முதல் இருந்து வரும் நீதி என்பார்.

at the poetry assembly held for the Golden Jubilee
poets who have taken the thread of imagination
Elders who have come to this hall

On Tamil New Year’s Day, 14 April 1990,
Chief Minister Kalaignar delivered on Madras Television
this presiding poem under the title
To the Tamil people filled with heartfelt love,
to the distinguished ones who have come to create lofty poetry,
and to my siblings dearer to me than life —
I heap my greetings and good wishes!
“Spit! Spit!! Why this fellow?” has changed;
now a time has come when they send for me —
For the assembly of poets gathered here,
Without drinking the mother’s milk called grammar,
I drank the bottled milk of modern verse —
to preside over a poetry assembly!
“vai kāsu,” “put down money” — for my poem.
They ask me to give my blessing
who has received her share in this poetry assembly;
to the Chithirai maiden born of Panguni,
they ask me to give my blessing.
because I will not offer a *Purattasi* —
With a half-sari that does not slip from the breast —
a woman of a traditional household,
Then she danced and stamped, *thai, thai*,
Because she said the first day of Thai
is the true Tamil New Year!
but to keep her from melting in anger,
if Tamils have two New Years in one year,
is that not twice the joy?
On the cool face of the tender maiden
Do not be startled and ask,
More than calling this merely a New Year,
I rejoice that this is the centenary year
lifted by the hand those who had lain
and spread sunlight across their faces —
that history, on this colourful festival,
To the one who gave the Constitution
to the one who stood tall as the Vindhyas
in this year when we celebrate their centenaries,
may the evil powers that torment us
The sage Vallalar of Vadalur said:
religion and the mire of scripture,
We have not honoured his words!
We only raise arches that hide the sky
and hold festivals for him — without shame!
that all lives are equal by birth —
but refuse to put his words into practice.
For the daughters and sons we ourselves beget,
inside the circles of relatives and caste.

about a principle they themselves will not live?
Why does the body burn with anger
There are Tamils in Tamil Nadu
who learned, long before Ettappan’s age,
to praise, worship and sing hymns to betrayal.
Even if Kattabomman spits at them,
those calculating men do not care —
to swear “Even if my throat is strangled,
to make even one of those claims real —
what use is it to climb a platform
and pose before the people as a great warrior?
Only when word and deed are one
we shall labour to increase prosperity;
we shall say that, like the linchpin of a chariot,
the nation must stand behind the plough;
and a society without longing and deprivation,
and build a clear, healthy life;
that if rulers move like a pouncing tiger,
that those whose backs were broken,
who drifted in education and employment
will in the coming age gain prosperity
that the poor young girl educated through eighth standard,
who once sighed that family life
was a fruit beyond her reach,
and that five thousand rupees to help place the *thali*

and cry out, crushed by poverty,
the sum given by the government
that children shall receive nutritious food with eggs;
that women must not be treated as mere hens;
that thirty per cent reservation is a first-stage concession,
and that in the end men and women must receive
that is, half and half, fifty per cent;
that only when women’s rights are secured
will the rights of the soil in this speaking land endure;
half shall belong to the daughter too —
a proud law of equal right;
that on three festivals each year
five kilograms of rice shall be free;
that not only Adi Dravidars and tribal people,
but also the most backward and denotified communities
that we shall work until there is no small village
with the sky as roof and the earth as mat —
we shall continue daily the plan
to build sturdy houses for fishers,
while defending the country and language
shall receive welfare funds and opportunities;
shall have their just demands heard,
and we shall leap to remove their suffering.
Not merely words sweet as jaggery —
that gives deeds a form for its words!
let us grow thought — let us act —
let us increase prosperity and guard character;
with the light of truth in the heart
I am a poet who gives freedom to poetry;
Those who come to sing upon them are
let the learned gain their chance;
of literary Tamil upon this earth!
let us touch the edge of the sky!
we would scoop and scoop without decrease

and give them a good life,
Now let us hear Arasu Manimekalai’s rare poem
The Kaveri has another name: Ponni!
how to act and solve that very problem,
Let us see what thought she gives us!

we hope she will give good ideas

Gandhi was the gift of time;

and with them, to stand on the path
a reader of news on television,
a man who breathes classical Tamil.
What will he say so that rights may be won?
the man of laughter in a poetry assembly —
not one who stands beside us
This steel poet comes to say:

So that the lion-like gathering of Tamil youth
and live lulled by gentle breezes!
increasing wealth alone your goal in life,

what we wear is two garments,”

items.titleEn: A Backwater Full of Ignorant Folk!

elements.text: A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
If the one or two decent people there grow alarmed
and rise to speak against them,
and throw them into the burning fire!
Are they not a gang grown fat and roaming free?
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
Knowing that little dogs will bark,
shut their mouths and trap them in the net!
A certain “Maya” in the middle of the hall
A trick learnt from the womb itself!
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
There is no useful plan to make the village prosper;
Maya's work is to cultivate corruption
so that she alone may live in splendour!
and they will flay your skin!
and still, because sleep has not cleared,
they beat the drum of swagger!
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
They say chaste Kannagi once blazed in fury
“Look, I too will burn something in return!”
and Panchali Devi burns a newspaper.
Even after propping a spine into their backs,
the fool-crowd, it seems, lies hunchbacked!
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
“I shall place this whole village on a leaf
and finish eating it, cooked and uncooked alike—
Even when that Maya says so,
to support her and fall at her feet!
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
Declaring contradiction itself to be scripture,
they say the drumstick tree is fit for building a house!
They say that if a wall of wax candles is raised as a fort,
fire itself will flee in fear and hide!
“I shall commit a thousand sins,” she says—
“God is on my side!” No, not even that:
“I myself am that God!” she says!
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
When everyone stands like hand-raising dolls,
and lifts left hand and right hand together,
would wicked Maya's delight not boil over?
Before it collapses like a long wall that cannot stand,
so that wickedness may swiftly be destroyed
A backwater full of ignorant folk—
and on its panchayat board, most of them are the same!
அரசின் பீர் தொழிற்சாலை விற்று இருகோடி சுருட்டுறார்.

Tamil Nadu is being looted, mother,

In olden days they tied up their hair,
built huts and lived as sages.
Even those men, who had not wholly renounced,
they preached what were called lofty principles.
Yet those who claim to have come in their path
and some have planted poisonous seed
have withered like a scorched sapling;
social progress has spilled onto the ground
Whoever says, “Come, I shall show you God,”
and calls you to the bed,
he says, “I shall show you heaven,”
As though that were a chapter of spirituality,
a crowd of women believes his desire to be worship.
Is being deceived a chapter—or an outrage?
How many mahatmas, how many Sai Babas,
how many miracles have they shown!
Though people know that a magician
can reproduce all of it in a moment on a stage,
what a cruelty that they still become
If one has received divine grace,
why dakshina, offerings and daily worship?
why rosewater to bathe every limb of his body?
Is the sign of having attained nakedness
that he delights in photographing women naked?
In place of staff and water-pot,
there gleam a sword and liquor;
there is a body fed and swollen,
Seeing all this again and again,
why does the crowd still remain
One ashram for printing counterfeit notes;

Those who set fire to a thatched house
A shawl is wrapped around a rat snake,

for piling up mountains of money,

To end the grief of childlessness,

covers her body with his own,

though such reports arrive in waves every day,

behind a screen of divinity will burn away!

let us beat the drum and set out,
like a pride of Tamil lions rising!
let us tear off the masks

rising with a shiver like leopards,

brother, did you hear that song

items.titleEn: Let Us Rise in the East Like the Sun!

elements.text: தாள் ஏந்தும் மனிதர்கட்கோ ஒரு துளியும் மானமில்லா காட்சி!!

நந்திக் கிடக்கின்றார் பணம், பதவி, சலுகைகளை; அவரெல்லாம்
நன்று நன்று, நீயேதான் திராவிடத்தின் தாயே என்கின்றார்,

தொழில் வரி, நிலவரி, பயிர் வரி என்று

Each day, when they turn the pages of the newspapers,
Tamil people writhe at news that stings like scorpions.
A rule that destroys the lives of the poor like a sword—
and what a sight: those who carry the papers
show not even one drop of shame!
Every day comes news of theft in temples;
even the idols of the Lord are stolen—
a red fire in devotees' hearts.
as food for the hunger of “Death”;
in police stations, rape and killings
we are not so ignorant as to say they do not.
must thousands upon thousands of police
line up and stand like motionless tall trees,
without even a mustard-seed of concern in the heart,
They certainly know how to curry favour—
for money, office and concessions say,
“Good, good—you alone are the Mother of Dravidianism!”
the quantity of ration rice shrinks sharply;
the cruelty of prices rises into a giant form;
Tamil people breathe out fire in long sighs!
and diesel, petrol and cooking-gas prices rising too,
the eyes of farmers burn with heat;
so do the eyes of those who labour beside them,
Professional tax, land tax, crop tax—
Seeing the acts of rulers who bring such distress,
spread their beds, sing and dance in delight;
they sit in the Fort and scold others!
To watch and endure all this—
or a burial ground, a cremation ground?
So, vowing that we shall endure no longer,
so that the country may live
with the ranks of our allied parties
To teach a lesson to the deceivers
the people who trusted them and voted,
a struggle on the path of nonviolence!
the arrow we launch will be a total shutdown!
We can lie down no longer.
let us rise in the east like the sun!
திருமாலும் பன்றி உருவெடுத்து திரைகடல் புகுந்து சென்றார்!

Rolling the earth itself up like a mat,

“I have fallen in love with you.”
